correctness.rationale: Three iterations of a radius-one cellular automaton have effective radius three. A 64-state de Bruijn walk records a six-bit overlap and appends a seventh bit only when the central output of Rule62^3 equals the original central input. Closed walks of length n therefore biject to labelled cyclic points fixed by f^3, even at short cyclic sizes by periodic closure. A separately generated 4-state one-step walk has characteristic polynomial x^3(x-1), hence tr(H^n)=1 for all n>=1 and exactly one temporally fixed state. Prime temporal period three gives C_n=(tr(M^n)-1)/3. Independent construction of M and exact SymPy characteristic polynomial factorization matches x^51(x-1)(x²+1)(x²-x-1)Q(x); the separate rational Schur-Cohn reduction in the source establishes |lambda_j|<3/2 and justifies the uniform exponential remainder. Fresh exhaustive ring tests for n=1..12 yield C_n=(0,0,1,0,5,7,7,24,22,35,77,87). Enumeration is corroboration, whereas transfer path correspondence and exact polynomial certificate establish all n.

But Stricker (2023) computes and classifies finite ring spectra only in finite sampled ranges; Taga et al. (2021) calculate ECA Koopman spectra at a fixed 13-cell size. No accessible exact all-length count or its golden-ratio rate was found; priority remains qualified by these plausible works.

value.rationale: An all-ring exact cycle census for a nonlinear elementary automaton yields an explicit rational dynamical zeta contribution, distinct spatial growth rate and finite-size spectral correction. It resolves a natural quantitative gap between finite-state period detection and asymptotic cycle abundance, without conflating spatial n with temporal period three.

final_claim: For Wolfram elementary binary cellular automaton Rule 62 on each labelled cyclic ring of length n>=1, the number C_n of distinct orbits of least temporal period exactly three is (tr(M^n)-1)/3, where the 64-state de Bruijn transfer M has characteristic polynomial x^51(x-1)(x^2+1)(x^2-x-1)Q(x) and Q(x)=x^8+x^7+x^6+x^5+3x^4+2x^3+x^2+2x+1. Therefore C_n=(phi^n+(-phi^-1)^n+2cos(pi*n/2)+sum_j lambda_j^n)/3=phi^n/3+O((3/2)^n), lambda_j roots of Q, phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. No assertion about all temporal periods or infinite-line entropy.
limitations: Only least temporal period 3 on labelled cyclic binary rings, not general temporal periods, infinite-space mixing or optimal spectral error.
The octic remainder O((3/2)^n) is certified but not claimed to be sharp.
